To streamline the step-free entrance accessibility feature, "Step-free path to the guest entrance" will be removed and combined with "Step-free guest entrance”, for one simplified feature called "Step-free access”. 
We will automatically update listings to only use the "Step-free access" accessibility feature. The migration begins on November 5, 2024 and lasts approximately one month. articles.description:
Incident began at 2024-10-30 12:30 and ended at 2024-10-30 18:46 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Incident Report

Summary

On 29 October 2024 some Gmail web users experienced slow loading, unresponsive or crashed web pages for a duration of 22 hours, 46 minutes

To our customers whose businesses were impacted during this outage, we sincerely apologize. This is not the level of quality and reliability we strive to offer you.

Root Cause

Browser extensions, such as third-party ones, have significant freedom to run their own JavaScript code on web pages they're active on. This means they can modify the page's appearance and content, interact with remote servers, and potentially even disrupt the page's functionality.

While extensions operate in their own isolated environment, they can technically access information from the main web page. However, the reverse isn't true, limiting the website's control over the extension's actions. Essentially, extensions have a wide range of capabilities with minimal oversight, potentially leading to unintended consequences or conflicts with the web page.

A recent update to a third-party browser extension resulted in some Gmail web users who have these extensions installed experiencing performance problems, such as increased latency or unresponsiveness.

Remediation and Prevention

Google engineers were alerted to the issue by internal monitoring on 30 October 2024 at 07:04 US/Pacific and immediately started an investigation. The issue was fully mitigated at 11:44 US/Pacific after the third-party mitigated the issue from their end.

Google is committed preventing a repeat of this issue in the future and is completing the following actions:

  • Implement testing for popular browser extensions to better detect and quickly mitigate similar issues.
  • Improve internal documentation/processes to enable faster response and mitigation time for this type of issue.

Detailed Description of Impact

Gmail

Customers using the Gmail Web UI may have experienced increased latency or unresponsiveness when also using certain third-party extensions.

Additional Information for Customers:

This issue only affected the Gmail Web UI. Gmail iOS/Android apps could be used as a workaround during the issue duration.

Affected products: Gmail
articles.title: RESOLVED: We're investigating reports of an issue with Gmail. We will provide more information shortly.

Oct 30, 09:42 UTC
Resolved - On October 30, 2024, between 5:45 and 9:42 UTC, the Actions service was degraded, causing run delays. On average, Actions workflow run, job, and step updates were delayed as much as one hour. The delays were caused by updates in a dependent service that led to failures in Redis connectivity. Delays recovered once the Redis cluster connectivity was restored at 8:16 UTC. The incident was fully mitigated once the job queue had processed by 9:24 UTC. This incident followed an earlier short period of impact on hosted runners due to a similar issue, which was mitigated by failing over to a healthy cluster.
From this, we are working to improve our observability across Redis clusters to reduce our time to detection and mitigation of issues like this one in the future where multiple clusters and services were impacted.  We will also be working to reduce the time to mitigate and improve general resilience to this dependency.
Oct 30, 08:48 UTC
Update - We are continuing to investigate delays to status updates to Actions Workflow Runs, Workflow Job Runs, and Check Steps. articles.description:
From 12:02 AM PDT to 1:19 AM PDT on Sunday, November 3, 2024, some users experienced trouble logging into Slack with SSO, provisioning users with SCIM, received duplicated notifications, and had trouble triggering workflows.

The system responsible for the handling of database replications and routing traffic had unexpected failures due to a time-logic configuration change. As a result, requests involving these database replicas timed out, impacting all SCIM operations, SSO logins, notification handling, and workflow execution.

As an immediate fix, we manually processed these database replications, restoring full functionality to the affected services. 

After verifying that requests were successfully serviced, we implemented a backend logic update to allow for future system changes to be handled automatically, reducing the likelihood of this reoccurring.
articles.title: Incident: Users unable to sign in with SSO or SCIM. Multiple Slack features are experiencing issues.

articles.description:
From October 31, 2024 4:30 PM PDT to November 1, 2024 3:30 AM PDT some users experienced issues with the date field in lists appearing garbled. 

We were able to trace this back to a code change that inadvertently caused the issue.

We reverted this code change which resolved the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with the date field in lists

articles.description:
From approximately 4:11 PM PDT to 4:13 PM PDT on Wednesday, October 30, 2024, some users experienced issues with essential functions like loading, connecting, and sending messages in Slack.

A recent backend change was intended to improve traffic and error handling. However, an unexpected configuration change during the rollout led to a temporary spike in connection errors.

We observed automatic recovery from the configuration change, which restored functionality to affected users. However, we reverted the problematic code that initially caused the issue.
articles.title: Incident: Connectivity issues in Slack

articles.description:
On Monday, October 28, 2024 around 2:29 PM PDT until 6:55 PM PDT, some users observed workflows containing steps that included some connectors such as Google Sheets, Slack lists, or Jira could not be saved.

We discovered there were missing components from a recent feature release causing the inability to save workflow steps. We adjusted the backend logic to include the missing components, restoring full functionality to affected workflow steps.
articles.title: Incident: Some workflows are unable to be saved.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From 3:19 PM PDT to around 4:02 PM PDT on October 24, 2024, lists were unavailable in Slack. Users may have come up against an error message or noticed that the feature was missing from the sidebar.

We accidentally deactivated the lists feature during the course of routine cleanup work. Once we realised this mistake, we immediately re-enabled lists for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Lists are unavailable for users

articles.description:
On October 15, 2024, from 12:00 PM PDT to 2:33 PM PDT, some workflows that utilize incoming webhooks to send messages returned the error “team_not_found”, and the messages weren’t shared to the intended channel.

We traced the issue back to a recent code change related to ensuring webhooks and plugins work as expected. The change didn’t account for a variable, which triggered the error.

Once we reverted the change and rolled out a fix, the issue was resolved for all affected workflows.
articles.title: Incident: Some webhooks are returning `team_not_found`

articles.description:
On Friday, October 18, from 10:00 AM PDT to 1:00 PM PDT some newly invited users reported receiving an "ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS" error when trying to login to workspaces using Single Sign On (SSO). 

We discovered the issue was related to a code change that handles traffic to our Terms of Service page, a feature only available on our enterprise plan. As a result, users were incorrectly redirected regardless of their workspace plan. We identified the problematic portion of code and reverted it. Once this completed, users reported being able to log in successfully.
articles.title: Incident: Newly invited users unable to login with SSO

articles.description:
From October 17, 2024 at 4:30 PM PDT to October 18, 2024 at 5:00 AM PDT, users experienced issues with creating Legacy Incoming Webhooks which resulted in "500 errors".

We were able to trace this back to a code change that inadvertently caused the issue.

We reverted this code change and rolled back to an earlier version, which has resolved the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Issues creating new Legacy Incoming Webhooks

articles.description:
From October 16th, 2024 at 10:05 PM PDT to 1:37 AM PDT October 17th, 2024, some users experienced issues with their user status.

Statuses couldn't be cleared, and the expiration reflected current time. In some cases, statuses had defaulted to "In a meeting".

We traced the issue back to a delay in the job queue that handles custom user status updates. 

Once we were able to clear the jobs causing the delay, we rolled out a fix resolving the issue for impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with custom statuses

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
Beginning on Tuesday, October 1, 2024 at 12:00 PM PDT, until 10:12 AM PDT on Monday, October 14, 2024, some Android users experienced an issue with their user status being shown incorrectly as well as a constant blue loading bar near the top of their app.

This issue was traced back to a bug that was introduced by incorrect logic with a feature flag. We rolled back the problematic feature flag, resolving the issue for all affected users. We are continuously making improvements to feature flag releases to reduce the likelihood of events such as these. Thank you for your patience.
articles.title: Incident: User status on Android may be showing incorrectly.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On Friday, October 11, 2024, from 4:08 AM PDT until 4:50 AM PDT, users experienced an issue with loading their threads, coming across a "Something's a bit fishy!" error message.

We traced this back to a performance issue with a backend database responsible for processing certain thread actions, resulting in requests not being served correctly.

To mitigate any immediate impact, an automated safety measure initiated the restart of the database services. This improved database performance, but the process took longer than expected, contributing to the errors users experienced. Once this process completed, threads began loading without error.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may have trouble loading threads.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From Friday, October 4th, at 3:10 PM PDT until Monday, October 7th, at 9:55 AM PDT, users encountered error code "REBBB58853E3" when they attempted to expand bulleted lists in Slack AI channel recaps.

We traced the issue to a recent change in backend logic that introduced errors when loading content within bulleted recaps.

A fix was deployed to correct the logic which resolved the issue for all users.
articles.title: Incident: Some users are seeing a channel recap error: REBBB58853E3
